item.title: Could the National Guard play a role in the Midterms?
item.description: The National Guard's presence has become routine in D.C., but there's nothing routine about questions over the role the troops could play in the upcoming midterms.

item.title: World's youngest museum curator, 11, was led by a love of fossils
item.description: NPR's Ailsa Chang speaks with Anderson Taylor, who has become the Guinness World Record holder for youngest male museum curator. He opened a natural history museum at age 9.
item.content:encoded: NPR's Ailsa Chang speaks with Anderson Taylor, who has become the Guinness World Record holder for youngest male museum curator. He opened a natural history museum at age 9.

item.title: Hit hard by the earthquake in western Colombia, the mayor of Cali gets to work
item.description: Search efforts continue though hopes are fading as teams dig for survivors from the 7.4 magnitude earthquake that killed more than 250 people.

item.title: Europe swelters through its fifth heatwave of the summer
item.description: Europe is sweltering through its fifth heatwave this summer. It has already lasted longer than a deadly heat wave that killed thousands across Europe in 2003.
item.content:encoded: Europe is sweltering through its fifth heatwave this summer. It has already lasted longer than a deadly heat wave that killed thousands across Europe in 2003.

item.title: Palestinians have no place to put their money. Officials warn a breakdown is looming
item.description: Palestinians in the West Bank have too much cash. Israeli banks refuse to accept their deposits and Palestinian authorities warn an economic breakdown is looming.

item.title: A summer canoe trip through New York's north woods to wild sand beaches
item.description: NPR's Brian Mann paddled the Ausable River in northern New York on a summer day to swim on wild sand beaches that stretch along Lake Champlain's shore.

item.title: AIPAC didn't always spend on campaigns. Now it faces criticism over money in politics
item.description: U.S. support for Israel has been a central issue in Democratic primary contests. That's put a spotlight on the pro-Israel lobbying group AIPAC and the strength of its political influence.

item.title: What the data says about the discourse around men, women and money
item.description: NPR's Juana Summers talks with Hanna Horvath, author of Your Brain on Money on Substack, about balance — or the lack thereof — in heterosexual relationships where women out-earn men.

item.title: Democratic socialism's next test is the Midwest
item.description: A democratic socialist narrowly lost Wisconsin's Democratic gubernatorial primary. But conversations with swing voters suggest voters may be more open to the "socialist" label than expected.
